name: Joshua Rotenberg
body: Your posting asks for someone who wants to shape a market rather than run launches, and who is as comfortable writing the messaging as defining the strategy. I should say plainly that I have not carried a Product Marketing title, and I have not worked in digital health. What I have done is the work underneath the title, in markets that did not have a playbook yet.

At Wix I was part of standing up a brand-new vertical that went from proof of concept to a profitable business line, and I built the sales training that equipped tenured account executives to sell into it. That is the part of your posting I recognize most: a segment nobody had defined yet, a value proposition that had to be written before anyone could sell it, and enablement that had to exist before the numbers moved. At Level Agency I ran integrated campaigns across inbound, paid, and content as the strategic lead, writing the landing pages and email sequences myself and then defending the results in QBRs. At Birdeye I equipped 15-20 reseller partners across health, home services, and retail with the positioning and health metrics they used to sell the product inside their own markets, and retained all but one.

The through-line is translation. At Solenzo, the company I founded, my daily work is turning complex automation and performance data into narratives that non-technical owners understand and act on, which is a smaller version of what you are describing with movement intelligence and clinical evidence. I would want to be honest in a first conversation about what a healthcare learning curve actually costs you, and to hear where you think the vertical strategy is hardest right now.
